analysis.title: GS Sector Specialists: U.S. Industrials & Materials (Ryan Novak, 2 Oct 2026): NFP preview, airlines Q3 EPS preview
key_insights: Desk morning note for Friday Oct 2. S&P futures are up 50bps early to close a volatile week. Attention is on the September payrolls report (NFP) and speeches by Fed's Logan and Goolsbee.

Macro watch: the French-German 10-year yield spread is widening toward 150bps, which the desk reads as signs of a growing crisis in France. Brazil's two presidential candidates are deadlocked in polls ahead of Sunday's election.
Commodities and rates paused: crude is down 3%, Brent is back below $100 and WTI is below $90. The 10-year yield is down to 5.22%, DXY is just below 92 and Bitcoin is up 2% to $86.4k.
NKE gave very weak fiscal 2027 topline guidance. The desk sees it as more company-specific than a broad comment on the consumer.

GIR NFP preview: payrolls estimated at +80k in September vs consensus +88k. Layoffs are low and big-data job indicators picked up. September payrolls tend to underperform when Labor Day falls late in the month, as it did this year, and August's jump was boosted by leisure/hospitality and local education hiring that GIR does not expect to repeat.
GIR expects the unemployment rate to edge down to 4.0% from 4.1% because continuing claims fell, and average hourly earnings up 0.2% m/m, below consensus, on negative calendar effects.
RTX won a $24.4bn multi-year contract for SM-6 interceptors, building on its existing agreements with the Department of War.

GT plans to close its chemical manufacturing plants in Niagara Falls and Bayport. Charges are $55-75mm, of which $30mm is cash ($35mm in Q3, $15mm in Q4). The company expects Americas segment operating income to improve by $15-20mm a year from 2027.
GVA was awarded the $325mm Big Creek Tunnel project in Ohio. BA averted a strike as workers ratified a new contract offer.
Next week's first Q3 earnings are DAL and RPM. The desk reflags longs in ETN, EXPD, PCAR, XPO and TT, with DOV, OC, GWW, AAL and CRH as sources of funds, going into Q3 EPS and year-end.

Airlines Q3 preview: carriers trimmed capacity to lift revenue against much higher fuel prices. Unit revenue (RASM) is forecast to accelerate from flat exiting 2025 to mid-teens growth in 3Q 2026, helped by a better competitive landscape.

Jet fuel rose significantly after the June low and is near 2026 highs. GS raised its jet fuel forecast materially, cut its 4Q 2026 industry outlook to about $250 million from $3.7 billion, and cut 2027 and 2028 industry net income forecasts by 28% and 24%.

GS highlights Buy-rated ALGT, with a smaller-than-industry cut to its FY 2026 forecast and what it expects to be one of the industry's leading 2027 margins, on less low-fare competition and merger synergies. ALGT trades at about 7.5x the reduced 2027 forecast vs a historical P/E average of about 14x.

sector_views.rationale: Strong unit revenue growth from capacity cuts is being offset by higher jet fuel. GS cut its 4Q 2026 industry outlook to about $250 million from $3.7 billion and its 2027 and 2028 net income forecasts by 28% and 24%. ALGT is the Buy-rated exception.

earnings_insights: NKE gave very weak fiscal 2027 topline guidance (already announced). The desk reads it as company-specific, not a broad consumer signal.
DAL and RPM report next week and are the first Q3 earnings of the season for this desk's coverage.
GT restructuring: $55-75mm total charges, $30mm in cash, $35mm in Q3 and $15mm in Q4. Americas segment operating income is expected to improve $15-20mm annually from 2027.

Airlines Q3 2026 preview (GS forecast): unit revenue (RASM) growth in the mid-teens, vs flat exiting 2025. GS cut its 4Q 2026 industry outlook to about $250 million from $3.7 billion on higher jet fuel (GS estimate).

GS cut its 2027 and 2028 industry net income forecasts by 28% and 24%, mainly on higher jet fuel. ALGT's FY 2026 forecast cut is smaller than the industry's, and it trades at about 7.5x GS's reduced 2027 forecast.
Earnings calendar this week: CCL and KMX pre-market and AIR post-market on 9/29, AYI pre-market on 10/1.
